thread:
sarah-sales: Hey team — AcadiaHealth POC kickoff. They want a Private deployment using PrivateLink into their VPC. Couple of asks: can we preserve client source IP to backend? They need a latency SLO ~120ms for inference. Also pricing question: if they run on Dedicated reserved capacity, how do we bill egress + private connector data transfer? Security wants the minimal outbound ports/FQDNs and any TLS-inspect guidance.

mike-netops: Short answer: PrivateLink by default terminates in our infra and you see our source IPs unless you deploy a connector/proxy inside the customer VPC. We have two common patterns:
- Connector inside customer VPC (sidecar VM/container) -> preserves client srcip and uses internal routing
- Default PrivateLink -> traffic egresses from Redwood and appears as our backend IPs (X-Forwarded-For added).

aj-platform: For the connector option we typically recommend colocating the connector in a private subnet with an ENI and a SG that allows outbound 443 to our control plane and 80/443 to model servers (if using internal proxy). The connector does NAT by default but can be configured to preserve src. We also inject X-Forwarded-For header on HTTP.

nina-security: For the security questionnaire: we need to provide the FQDNs and IP ranges to allow. Also list of approved TLS ciphers and whether TLS-inspect will break SNI. If the customer uses TLS inspection, they must keep a passthrough for model traffic or we need certs on the proxy.

sarah-sales: Can you paste a minimal firewall snippet + what to tell their NetOps to test? They asked for a one-pager to hand to infra.

mike-netops: Sure — minimal egress for connector mode (customer VPC -> our service):
```
# Allow outbound from connector instances
# control plane (api, auth): tcp/443 to control.redwood-inference.com (FQDN resolves to dynamic IPs)
# inference endpoints (TLS): tcp/443 to model-X.redwood-inference.com (FQDN list we provide)
# optional healthchecks: tcp/443 to health.redwood-inference.com

# Example security group egress rules:
Type    Protocol    Port Range    Destination
HTTPS   TCP         443           0.0.0.0/0  # or restrict to Redwood IP list when provided
NTP     UDP         123           169.254.169.123/32  # if needed for time sync (opt)
```

Also, if they want to preserve client-src IP end-to-end, they must route egress from their app to the connector locally rather than hitting PrivateLink endpoint directly. Otherwise our backend will see connector IPs. We can provide an appliance image if they want an AMI.

aj-platform: On pricing: Dedicated reserved capacity billing covers model inference compute. Network egress outside the Dedicated cluster (e.g., traffic between customer and Redwood control plane, or between connector and Redwood public endpoints) is billed as outbound egress units on the contract. For Private deployments where the connector sits in-customer, there is typically no extra per-token network fee from us, but cloud egress charges on their side still apply. If they want us to route through our peered egress (we can offer a managed egress path) that adds a predictable per-GB fee — we can include that in the PO.

ops-oncall: Quick gotcha: if they have an IPSec/SD-WAN path, expect MTU drops. Recommend MTU 1400 on the connector instances to avoid fragmentation for IPsec with 1500-site endpoints. Also watch TCP MSS clamping on the network appliances.

sarah-sales: Great — can we give them an explicit test plan so NetOps can validate connectivity and latency?

mike-netops: Test plan (simple):
1) From a bastion in their VPC run: `curl -v --resolve model-test.redwood-inference.com:443:10.0.5.10 https://model-test.redwood-inference.com/health` (replace with connector IP or PrivateLink ENI). Expect 200 and TLS chain.
2) Run 1 minute RPS test: `wrk -t2 -c10 -d60 https://model-test.redwood-inference.com/predict` and capture p50/p90 latency.
3) Verify source IP: hit an echo endpoint we provide and check the REMOTE_ADDR and X-Forwarded-For.

nina-security: For the questionnaire answers: include these bullets:
- TLS: TLS1.2+ required, recommend TLS1.3 where supported.
- Ciphers: ECDHE suites only.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported for Private deployments (we support AWS KMS + BYOK via HSM).
- Audit: request_id and per-request audit logs retained per contract.
- TLS inspection: if the customer performs TLS inspection, they must allow passthrough for model traffic or provide certs we can install on their proxy.

sarah-sales: Perfect. Any enterprise blockers we should flag? They asked about SLA for latency and multi-AZ redundancy.

aj-platform: SLA notes — Dedicated has latency-backed targets per route and we can set canaries. For Private deployments inside a VPC we can offer multi-AZ connector placement and HA clusters. The hard blocker is cross-account PrivateLink where the customer mandates source-ip preservation without any connector — that's not supported. You either accept XFF or deploy our connector inside their account.

mike-netops: Another potential blocker: corporate proxies that rewrite Host headers or strip SNI. If they have TLS-inspect that terminates TLS and re-encrypts with a corporate cert, that will break certificate pinning unless allowed. Document that in the security answers.

ops-oncall: For the customer's latency SLO of <120ms — we need a sample dataset run. In my experience, model selection + sequence length dominate latency. Recommend we run their prompt set during POC on Dedicated instance with pinned model to validate. We'll include model knob suggestions (batch size, kv-cache TTL) to meet p50/p90 targets.

sarah-sales: I'll send this one-pager to the customer and ask for their NetOps contact + a test bastion. Can someone add the precise FQDN/IP allowlist and AMI link for connector in the doc?

aj-platform: I'll assemble the allowlist and AMI link and drop into the Confluence doc by EOD.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: redwood-poc-acadia-conn-v1 -> deploy started (canary).

sarah-sales: Thanks all — will ping once they confirm bastion access. :thumbsup:
